findings.title: Abstraction boundary is still implicit
findings.body: The implementation exposes storage-specific details through the domain API, which makes the task harder to reason about and weakens the DDD boundary.
findings.suggested_action: Introduce an explicit domain-level hint type and keep provider-specific details in adapters.

findings.title: Hypothesis test is underspecified
findings.body: The test evidence proves JSON parsing, but it does not state the falsifiable behavior that should fail if the review doctrine contract regresses.
findings.suggested_action: Add a fixture that fails when required objective or gate evidence is absent.

notes: The changed behavior matches the stated task contract.
Names and module boundaries are readable enough for future changes.
Storage and domain concepts need a clearer interface boundary.
The fixture includes regression coverage for doctrine validation.
The test evidence still proves JSON parsing more than the actual operator workflow.
The current fixture should state the falsifiable property more directly.
The typed contract compiles across the Rust workspace.
No formal proof obligation was introduced, but the reviewer recorded why it is not required.
The contract names use task graph and review doctrine language consistently.
Domain contracts stay serializable and side-effect free.
The objective and gate IDs have stable meaning independent of a runner implementation.
The reviewer flags unnecessary abstraction without asking for broad generated layers.
The available tests do not yet prove the end-to-end operator workflow.
Domain and adapter boundaries were reviewed.
Reviewer checked for generated bulk and abstraction debt.

unification_summary: The critic accepts the direction but requests an actor retry for abstraction and hypothesis-testing evidence before goal satisfaction.
